observations.title: Kilauea volcano (United States)
observations.description: The Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO) reported that the eruption within Kilauea?s Kaluapele summit caldera, characterized by incandescence, intermittent spatter, lava fountaining, and lava flows from vents along the SW and W margins of Halema`um`u Crater, continued at variable levels during 11-18 November. Incandescence persisted at both the N and SW vents at variable levels during the week. Flames and spatter bursts occasionally occurred at both vents. On 18 November scientists conducted a helicopter overflight and observed high levels of lava in each vent, with a roiling lava pond in the SW vent. The opening of the N vent was about 15 m in diameter and appeared to narrow at a depth of about 15 m, and the opening of the SW vent was elongate, and about 20 m long and 15 m wide. The Volcano Alert Level remained at Advisory (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) and the Aviation Color Code remained at Yellow (the second lowest color on a four-color scale). Source: US Geological Survey Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO)
